moments.title: The Savoy complex opens
moments.text: The Savoy Ballroom opened on Thanksgiving night 1927 on South Parkway at 47th St, part of a block that would include the Regal.

moments.title: The Regal opens
moments.text: The ornate movie palace at 4719 S. South Parkway, designed by Edward Eichenbaum, opened in the heart of Bronzeville, a stretch called the "Harlem of Chicago."

moments.title: A top stop for Black stars
moments.text: Ella Fitzgerald, Lena Horne and Duke Ellington were among the stars who played the Regal; Fitzgerald had an engagement in February 1952. Nat King Cole is said to have gotten his start at one of its amateur nights.

moments.title: The Jackson 5 open for Motown
moments.text: The young Jackson 5 opened for Gladys Knight & the Pips and Bobby Taylor & the Vancouvers. The theater closed around 1968, though some sources say 1971.

moments.title: A new cultural center
moments.text: The Harold Washington Cultural Center, named for Chicago's first Black mayor, opened at 4701 S. King Dr, on what it describes as the Regal's ground.

moments.title: Today: 47th St and King Dr
moments.text: The Harold Washington Cultural Center stands at the corner, near the Regal's old address.

checked.notes: Opened Feb 4, 1928 at 4719 S. South Parkway (now King Dr), designed by Edward Eichenbaum (Wikipedia, Cinema Treasures; one source says Levy and Klein, one says 4710). Closed about 1968 (or 1971), demolished 1973. Jackson 5 dates Aug 12 to 27, 1968; Fitzgerald Feb 10, 1952 (Chicago Public Library index); Ellington's appearances are lightly supported (WTTW). Nat King Cole's amateur-night start is a single-source claim. Harold Washington Cultural Center opened Aug 2004 on the Regal site per the center and Wikipedia; a Cinema Treasures commenter disputes the exact site. Address made specific. The story's 'Jackson 5 played its stage' kept.
